summary: Validated update (valid; single effect: executions of the recovery-value family fact). It attaches the receipt that first measured the status-guard path - 9b8471479d484a12bdaf961653bbbe54, with the same indices the status-guard question's own account binds to that claim: the peer holding the instance COMMITTED, the prepare reply reporting it together with the command, and the recovery's proposal and resulting states - so clause (c) of the fact no longer rests only on the retry receipt. Statement, conditions, sources and every other citation are unchanged. On the run: I attempted to close with the schema's stop mechanism (bounded_completed) and the controller declined it, since an open audit continues useful investigation until its own limits, so I used the remaining interval on the citation gap I had just found rather than on further wording churn. State of the work: six questions, all explained and receipt-backed - the fabricated-self-ballot value adoption up to a completed contradiction of a live replica's committed value; the equal-ballot empty-slice replacement decided by the reply adopted at the slow-quorum trigger position, measured across all six permutations of the three-reply set and four orders of a two-carrier/two-empty set and final because only N - SlowQuorumSize replies can follow; the status-guard stall cleared only by the executor's retry; recovery authority bounded by the recoverer's fixed ballot with no repair on the rejection path; the client-completion contract holding for the single-NOOP case but not the empty batch; and the wrong-row write in handlePreAccept refuted as unreachable. Ten receipts, six registered source materials covering the recovery and executor paths, both facts and all behaviour entries mutually consistent, and the captured source tree untouched. The directions I would pursue next, none of which is needed to support a stated conclusion, are a non-owner recoverer driving the delivery-order variant, a batch with several commands, and a run that drives the executor over a zero-length batch.
